# IdeaVim fixtures this host does not match yet.
#
# Generated by VimFixtureReplayTest, which writes the current list to
# build/fixture-failures.txt with the difference for each one, and a header saying how many were
# harvested and why the rest were not. To update this file, read that one and copy the names across
# - never edit a name by hand to make the build pass.
#
# 1034 of the 1049 harvested fixtures pass. These fifteen are grouped by what is actually wrong,
# which is seven things.
#
# The corpus grew by 24 when the harness stopped refusing fixtures with more than one caret, and
# twelve of those twenty-four failed. Four have been fixed since; the eleven left below are the
# eight that were already here plus what remains of the twelve. That is the yield of removing a
# refusal, and it is why refusing is only ever a temporary answer: multiple cursors are the feature
# VS Code is best known for.
#
# Four entries left this list without anything being fixed, which is the other thing to remember
# about it: the harness was typing setup commands through `parseKeys`, so `:nmap <Tab> ihello<Esc>`
# pressed Escape on the command line instead of writing five characters into it. Four fixtures had
# been recorded here as bugs in this host that were bugs in the harness reading them.

# --- Carets the engine narrowed away and this host kept.
#
# `<C-V>khV` leaves a block for line Visual and answers `expected [46], actual [46, 75]`; `Ve<C-G>`
# switches to Select mode with `expected [19, 104], actual [19, 42, 104]`; `g<C-H><S-Down>` gives
# `expected [12], actual [2, 12]`. Every one is a caret too many, and always when the selection
# changes *kind* without leaving Visual mode - which is the one path that does not go through
# `exitVisualMode`, where the engine drops the secondary carets itself.
#
# Sibling of the bug that was fixed here rather than the same one. That was about which caret is
# primary after a block is laid out; this is about which carets should still exist when the block
# stops being one.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/select/SelectToggleVisualModeHandlerTest.kt:test switch to select mode linewise multicaret
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/updown/MotionShiftDownActionHandlerTest.kt:test block select to empty line
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleLineModeActionTest.kt:enter visual line from visual block with motion up

# --- Select mode, where the caret sits on the other side of the selection.
#
# Four of these, and they agree with each other. `g<C-H>` enters block Select and puts the caret at
# the anchor here rather than at the far end (`expected [99], actual [12]`); `<C-V>bjj<C-G>` toggles
# a leftward block into Select and moves only the primary (`expected [15, 46, 87], actual [21, 52,
# 87]` - the last is right and the other two are six columns adrift, which is the width of the `b`).
# Select mode puts the caret *after* the selection where Visual puts it on the last character, and
# this host applies that to one caret rather than all of them.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/leftright/MotionShiftLeftActionHandlerTest.kt:test multiline with empty line block mode
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/search/SearchEntryFwdActionTest.kt:search in one time from select mode
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/select/SelectEnableBlockModeActionHandlerTest.kt:test entering select mode multicaret
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/select/SelectToggleVisualModeHandlerTest.kt:test switch to select mode blockwise left motion

# --- `1v`, which re-enters Visual over the size of the last one, per caret.
#
# `<C-V>jld1v` passes now. `<C-V>jld1v<ESC>kh1v` does not: `expected [16, 45], actual [15]`, one
# caret where there should be two. The size of the last Visual area is stored per caret, in
# `vimLastVisualOperatorRange`, and a caret that this host built fresh has none - so the second `1v`
# has nothing to rebuild the block from.
#
# `vedx1v` is the same field seen from the text side: the two carets delete different amounts.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleCharacterModeActionTest.kt:test enter visual with count after block visual operation multiple time


# --- An IntelliJ action replayed by `.`, which this host has no equivalent of.
#
# `c<C-End><C-I><esc>.` repeats a change that ran an IDE action in the middle of it. Arrived with
# the multi-caret fixtures because its `after` carries two selection markers.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/RepeatActionTest.kt:repeat command with execution of ij action

# --- One each.
#
# `ideajoin` is IntelliJ's smart join, a language feature this host cannot have.
#
# `partial Action mapping` is the keys of a half-typed `<Action>` mapping, replayed as literal text
# here instead of being recognised.
